transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-09-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Natalie Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Patel (Redwood SE), Lucas Meyer (Redwood CSM), Dr. Priya Rao (Marigold Head of ML), Marco Silva (CTO), Anna Berg (Infra), Kenji Ito (Security)

Summary (auto): quick recap of usage, ask for EU VPC template, move toward 1yr renewal + Dedicated uplift of 6 nodes, pilot timeline discussed.

[00:00] Natalie (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we have about 50 minutes, wanted to run through the renewal ask and the eu vpc / onprem pilot that priya flagged last week
[00:14] Dr. Priya Rao: yep, thanks natalie, quick context — model inference for diagnostics has doubled q/q, cost is creeping up, and some inference paths need sub-80ms p99 in eu for patient workflows, so we're exploring dedicated capacity in eu and a small on prem pilot for edge sites
[00:34] Marco (Customer/CTO): and key thing — data residency, we need logs to stay in eu, plus our legal wants KMS keys under our control, so any solution has to support customer-managed encryption
[00:52] Omar (Redwood SE): totally, thats in the private offering — we support KMS and HSM integrations for private deployments and vpc with customer KMS via our KMS bridge, though last mile network setup varies by cloud
[01:10] Anna (Infra): small note, our firewall team will want specific CIDR ranges, and we have strict egress rules; can you confirm whether traffic is routed through Redwood control plane or stays inside our VP C?
[01:30] Lucas (Redwood CSM): quick answer — for EU VPC the control plane is multi-tenant but we offer tenancy and audit log export; data plane for private deployments stays in-customer network. For VPC we do route control-plane telemetry out but tokens and payloads can be kept inside the VPC per the template
[01:50] Kenji (Security): are you SOC2 certified? we need evidence and a quick runbook of what audit logs look like, and SSO/SAML integration details
[02:05] Natalie: yes we have SOC2 Type II, i'll attach the report; and omar will attach the SAML SSO integration steps and the audit log schema
[02:20] Dr. Priya: on capacity numbers, our baseline today is ~120 qps with bursts to 350 qps for short windows. We want capacity for steady state plus room for growth — thinking about 6 dedicated nodes in eu, with burst to hosted api for spiky loads. what are the latency and cost tradeoffs?
[02:46] Omar: ok so with 6 dedicated nodes assuming our LLM runtime and your average seq len (you mentioned 256 tokens), you should expect 20-40ms lower p99 compared to hosted at same region due to dedicated GPU locality and consistent batching. Cost per-token will be higher for dedicated commit but unit-cost with sustained throughput actually drops because of KV cache warmness and batching across your traffic. i'll share numbers after we run a short benchmark
[03:16] Marco: benchmark — what do you need from us? sample requests or synthetic?
[03:22] Omar: ideally a tokenized sample of typical production requests, 30 minutes of representative traffic, plus a small prompt set for p99 sensitive endpoints. if that's hard, synthetic traces with seq len and qps distribution also work
[03:38] Anna: we'll put together the network doc, but we need a template VPC peering and egress plan, and an SOW for the EU VPC onboarding window — we have change freeze windows later this quarter
[03:54] Natalie: understood, we'll send the EU VPC architecture diagram and onboarding SOW template. we'll also include recommended firewall rules and nicknames for the routes
[04:06] Speaker 1 (possible mislabel): quick Q from kenji — how are keys rotated for the KMS bridge? and can we audit key usage?
[04:18] Kenji (Customer): yeah i'm asking — our compliance requires rotation every 90 days and an auditable trail that shows which keys were used to decrypt tokens
[04:28] Omar: the KMS bridge supports rotation policies and we forward kms operation logs to your audit subject or to your log export endpoint; we can support sending cloudkms/audit logs to your splunk or siem
[04:44] Dr. Priya: ok good. about the private onprem pilot — some of our hospitals need <50ms p99 and are on local infra; can we do a tiny onprem appliance or is it too heavy?
[05:00] Omar: there are two paths: lightweight onprem with our dedicated runtime in a containerized package (suitable for 1-2 nodes) or a full private cluster on your hardware. the lightweight option gives faster turnaround but fewer ops guarantees; the full cluster is more productiony and integrates with your KMS/HSM
[05:25] Marco: how long to get the lightweight pilot up? we have a month window where we can deploy in staging nodes
[05:33] Lucas: typical pilot installs in 2-4 weeks if firewall and network requirements are cleared. the critical path is the network and cert/key provisioning
[05:45] Anna: our infra team likes terraform templates; can you provide IaC snippets for the VPC and peering?
[05:55] Omar: yes, we'll include terraform snippets in the onboarding repo; small caveat — cloud provider-specific bits (like peering APIs) need minor edits per account
[06:08] Dr. Priya: on the financials — we're looking at a 12-month renewal with a 15% uplift in committed capacity over current baseline; also need clarity on break clauses if third-party models change licensing mid-term
[06:24] Natalie: we'll propose a 12-month renewal with an option to increase nodes at the mid-term review, and a clause for model licensing variance — we'll highlight fallback model tiers and cost protections in the quote
[06:38] Marco: are there penalties for early termination if we decide to go fully on-prem after 6 months?
[06:44] Natalie: standard early termination fees apply; however for strategic pilots we sometimes include a credit towards on-prem transition if you commit to a multi-year plan — i'll note that as a negotiable point
[06:58] Kenji: SSO, quick thing — we need SCIM provisioning and role-based access control maps. can your RBAC sync with our existing LDAP groups?
[07:10] Omar: yes, we support SCIM and can map LDAP groups to RBAC roles in the console. there's a small integration step to ensure group IDs match, we'll outline that in the SAML/SCIM doc
[07:24] Dr. Priya: can we see an example of the token-level cost breakdown per route? our finance team wants to understand per-model spend across different endpoints
[07:36] Lucas: good ask — we have token-level cost exports and per-route dashboards in the console. i'll attach a sample export and a dashboard snapshot; we can also set up a brief walkthrough with finance
[07:48] Anna: what about data retention? our policy requires 30-day retention in eu only, and all logs must be deletable on demand
[07:57] Omar: retention is configurable for private deployments and VPC; for hosted we have controls but limited if you use shared endpoints. we'll include the retention settings in the SOW and show how to purge logs via API
[08:12] Marco: ok i'd also like to understand fallback policies — if dedicated nodes are saturated, how fast does Redwood route to hosted variants and what's the impact on latency?
[08:24] Omar: our smart routing can failover in seconds; the tradeoff is you might see an increase in p99 (hosted region latencies slightly higher), but we can set thresholds and warm cache strategies to reduce cold-start hits
[08:40] Dr. Priya: i'd want to see a controlled failover test as part of pilot, to measure degraded latency and correctness of outputs
[08:50] Natalie: we'll add a failover runbook and a test plan to the pilot scope.
[09:00] Speaker 2 (automated note): action items documented, sending recording and notes after the call
[09:06] Marco: quick numbers question — if we go with 6 dedicated nodes, what's the expected monthly commit and an example cost delta vs current hosted spend?
[09:18] Omar: rough estimate on current telemetry you provided — monthly commit for 6 nodes in eu would be approx €XXk, with per-token unit cost lower by ~18-25% for steady traffic. exact quote to follow after benchmark
[09:36] Dr. Priya: ok we need that quote by next monday so procurement can start paperwork
[09:42] Natalie: we'll aim to deliver the quote and the SOW by 2028-09-17, along with SOC2 and SSO docs
[10:00] Anna: last operational Q — do you support private peering vs public egress and can egress be limited to a set of IPs?
[10:12] Omar: yes, private peering is supported and egress can be locked down to the IP ranges in the onboarding doc; some cloud vendors need express routes but we documented those patterns
[10:28] Kenji: and for the audit trail, we'd like to receive a sample of the log schema — especially anything that ties request IDs to key usage for audits
[10:38] Lucas: will attach the audit log schema and example exports.
[10:46] Dr. Priya: timeline recap — if we get the benchmark sample and network docs this week, pilot kickoff late september sounds feasible
[10:56] Natalie: perfect — to recap next steps: redwood sends SOW + VPC template + SOC2 + SAML/SCIM docs by monday; customer shares tokenized trace + firewall rules by thursday; schedule pilot kickoff 9/25-9/29.
[11:18] Marco: thanks all, appreciate the clarity. i'll loop in procurement and infra.
[11:26] Natalie: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the packet.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker mislabels (Speaker 1/2), occasional mistranscription of acronyms (VP C / VPC), and slight punctuation issues in timestamps.
